claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater plastic strain than pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater toughness than pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
Sluggish diffusion is characteristic of the WTaTiVZr high-entropy matrix.
Sluggish diffusion promotes the formation and retention of uniformly dispersed fine precipitates in WTaTiVZr.
The WTaTiVZr microstructure activates grain-boundary sliding at high temperature.
Fine precipitates and grain-boundary sliding facilitate dislocation motion.
Fine precipitates, enhanced dislocation motion, and controlled grain-boundary sliding retard crack initiation and propagation.
Elevated-temperature refractory high-entropy alloys can exhibit stable microstructures and substantial plasticity.
Dislocation motion can influence segregation during hot deformation of a refractory high-entropy alloy.
Pure tungsten lacks the stabilized phase distribution proposed for WTaTiVZr.
WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten will be compared after processing to comparable grain sizes and initial microstructural states.
In situ high-temperature SEM/TEM testing will monitor dislocations, grain-boundary sliding, precipitate evolution, and cracking during deformation.
The two materials will be tested under identical temperature, strain-rate, loading, and environmental conditions.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit higher plastic strain at failure than pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit more crack deflection or bridging than pure tungsten.
Pure tungsten will show limited plastic deformation and more brittle fracture than WTaTiVZr.
The proposed mechanism applies only where diffusion and grain-boundary mobility are active but precipitate coarsening and phase instability remain limited.
The mechanism is mainly applicable to single-phase refractory high-entropy alloys in a similar compositional family.
Controlled thermal treatments that alter precipitate state and grain-boundary character can test whether those features correlate causally with mechanical performance.
Failure to obtain statistically significant plastic-strain and toughness improvements, or failure to observe the proposed mediators, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The mediator and mechanism require a dispersed precipitate or stabilized phase distribution, which ordinarily implies multiple phases, while the boundary says the mechanism mainly applies to single-phase refractory alloys.

The initial-state and baseline fields call for comparable overall microstructural states, but the prediction requires fine precipitates in WTaTiVZr and their absence in tungsten. The matching criterion therefore needs clarification so that the proposed mediator is not inadvertently matched away.
